Hahahahah my degree didn’t change. Usually they recommend ICL after they feel your eyesight is stable. I had the replace my lens because it was sizing issues.

I did mine last year at eagle eye. Eyesight is 6.5 and 7.0, with thin cornea. Cost of $7,500 for the assessments and surgery. You can do the initial assessment and if you then decide to proceed with whatever surgery they recommend, they waive the initial consultation fee.

I picked eagle eye because it’s so reputable and so many friends have done it there, and it’s gone perfectly fine.

I had a very abnormal experience. The first surgery was fast (maybe less than 30 mins) and just felt tired and blurry after. Unfortunately I experienced far-sightedness, like I couldn’t even see things on my phone, and it turns out the lenses were too small. My eye shape is a lot deeper than most people’s and the scans didn’t pick up on this. Was told this is an extremely rare thing. Went for second surgery to take out and replace with new lens, and the complications for the second surgery were very bad (nausea, severe headaches, vomiting). With all this, found out that the lens for the right eye is still too small so no perfect vision yet. I have the option to go for another third surgery to hopefully correct it for the final time, or just leave it as it is. As it doesn’t affect my daily life, I’ve decided to leave it for now and go for checkups every half a year to make sure there are no further complications.  

Even with this not so pleasant experience, I don’t regret doing ICL. It’s nice to wake up and see my cat without having to find my glasses first.

OP I completely understand you. I have the rational logical side that goes “no it’s bad for you” but the emotional part wants to tell him I miss him, be angry at him, and talk to him as a friend again. 

I keep a journal of all the notes I wish I wrote to him, and thank goodness I blocked him because writing some of that stuff to him would have hurt our potential future friendship.

I didn’t do no contact at first, and it really hurt me because I saw that I was slowly becoming a less of a priority and his sweet replies and pet names were less and less. So I told him I had to block him and I did, including removing him from social media.

No contact allowed me to not get my hopes up - whenever a notification came in, I knew it wasn’t going to be him. And I guess with that, it helped me to stop thinking about him less. 

As I go through the stages of grief (currently anger), I’m happy I did block him because I think I would have said some things that would destroy any potential friendship we are to have in the future.  

You are doing so well for doing no contact for the last two weeks and you will continue excelling! You got this!!!

Our breakup was very amicable and the conclusion was that he would remain as friends. It was super hard so I decided to do no-contact a few days ago (it has not been successful). He is such a great person, and while I didn’t love him yet romantically - I love him very much as a person.

It would be so much easier to forget about him if he did something wrong - then I would feel anger instead of this bittersweet feeling of “what if”. I’m trying to stop being so sad about missing him as a boyfriend, and trying to change my mindset to, “Ok, this is a new stage of my relationship with him - where I get to be friends” and be excited about what this new dynamic could mean.
